key_insight: A subject-independent machine learning pipeline using acoustic speech features can detect Parkinson's disease with high accuracy while remaining interpretable through SHAP.
clinical_relevance: Speech-based biomarkers offer a non-invasive, scalable screening signal for early Parkinson's detection and may help reduce false positives in triage settings.
method: 756 voice recordings from 252 subjects were z-score normalized after preprocessing.
Five classifiers were compared under GroupKFold cross-validation: KNN, XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, and Naive Bayes.
SHAP was used to identify the most influential acoustic features for individual predictions.
evidence_signal: In subject-independent evaluation, KNN performed best with 92.10% accuracy, 94.50% F1 score, and 98.09% precision.
watch_item: Performance was reported on a single public dataset, so external validation across independent cohorts and recording conditions is still needed.
paper_title: An Explainable AI-Driven Classification Framework for Parkinson's Disease Detection via Acoustic Speech Features: A Comparative Machine Learning Study
